The board leans bear at the ACT rung, with the loose-conditions regime flag, the JPY haven cluster, and credit-SPX correlation all closest to joining in. Against that, the VIX-backwardation-x-credit setup is already firing bull, so you have a tactical washout signal pulling against a slower late-cycle warning, and that tension is the whole trade.

To turn the bear read into action you need the JPY leg of the T1 x JPY pair to come in alongside the alert cluster in SKEW, VIX9D, dealer gamma and the breadth jaws, which would stack a real risk-off regime on top of the complacency flag. What kills the bear idea is the T1 x HYG long paying off cleanly, credit repairing, and the on-alert list dropping back without any of the closest-to-firing conditions actually tripping.

Confluence over 8 weeks bear vs bull
Four rungs, and you only act on the top one. STAND DOWN, nothing is on. WATCH, one or two signals are true but they stand alone. SETUP, several are lining up. ACT, three of them have held for three sessions and they come from three different families, so it is not the same idea counted three times. A signal only counts once it has held three sessions, because one day in the zone is noise. Signals our lab rejected are left out of the count.
The three counts: firing = the condition is true at today's close, confirmed = it has been true 3 sessions in a row (this is what the bar counts), building = not true yet but close.
How to read each row: every signal is a checklist. Most of them need several things to be true at the same moment, so each line shows the condition, where it stands now and what it needs. A signal fires only when every box is ticked, which is why a number can sit well past its own trigger while the row still reads BUILDING. Some signals have two paths, either one arms them. ALERT (red bear / green bull) = it just fired, BUILDING = getting close, QUIET = nothing here yet. Widening? tells you whether the divergence is still growing or easing back. Dealer gamma is the plumbing read: negative means dealers sell weakness and buy strength, the fast-market rug-pull regime; positive means they do the opposite and you get the slow bid-the-dip grind. Net dealer gamma below zero is in place and has been for several sessions, so you're in the rug-pull regime now.

We haven't formally backtested this row, so it isn't a trigger: it's the regime filter that tells you to size moves bigger and respect air pockets on the downside. A flip back above zero puts you back in melt-up mechanics and changes how every other signal on this board should be played.

Kerberos said

This one fires when the VIX curve inverts while high-yield credit is taking a visible hit inside the same week, the kind of joint stress that marks forced selling rather than a slow bleed. Both legs are in place and the Kerberos composite reads it bull, meaning the panic has already done its work.

What kills the long read here is credit refusing to repair while the VIX curve re-steepens, which would turn the setup into a failed washout. Until then the historical pull higher over the next few months is the base case, and the fragile-flag caveat from the lab means you lean in without betting the account.

Statuses recompute nightly from the EOD pipeline. Confirmed = 3 consecutive sessions in zone (the framework buffer rule: one day in zone is noise). In formation = consecutive sessions spent in the top quintile of the metric. Sources: Polygon cache, nightly signal history tables, Yahoo for index series, FRED for macro. Grey rows are conditions Kerberos tracked that we cannot source yet; they stay listed so the catalog remains complete. Our own backtest verdicts live inside each row's detail.
